body.statement:
Fix an admissible boundary sequence satisfying \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\), \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\), and \(\limsup_n n\kappa_n^3<\infty\).  The schedule-quantified failure statement is true, but it does not certify a sharp \(n\kappa_n^3\) threshold.  For every deterministic schedule \(t_n>0\) with \(t_n\to0\), there is an experiment \(\mathbb P^{(t)}\in\mathfrak P_\kappa^0\); one may use the same \(2\times2\) experiment for all schedules, with \(p_n=r_n=(\kappa_n,1-\kappa_n)\), \(\Delta_n=0\), and all response means equal to \(\lambda/n\), where \(0<\lambda<-\log\alpha\).  It satisfies
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{\mathbb P^{(t)}}\!\left\{
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}
\leq1-e^{-\lambda}<1-\alpha.
\]
The same failure also occurs when \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\); its cause is the permitted response boundary and a vanishing critical value, not rare-margin optimal-face localization.
body.proof_tex:
Fix the boundary sequence and an arbitrary schedule \(t\).  Choose \(0<a<\lambda<-\log\alpha\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), set
\[
p_n=r_n=(\kappa_n,1-\kappa_n),
\qquad
\pi_{n,cx}=\frac14,
\qquad
\mu_{n,cx}=\frac{\lambda}{n}
\quad(c,x\in\{1,2\}).
\tag{28}
\]
Complete the finitely many initial rows arbitrarily subject to the floor conditions; the question presupposes that the experiment class is nonempty.  Since \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\), (28) obeys both floors eventually, and finite initial completion gives \(\mathbb P^{(t)}\in\mathfrak P_\kappa^0\).  Moreover,
\[
\Delta_n=\frac{\lambda}{n}-\frac{\lambda}{n}
-\frac{\lambda}{n}+\frac{\lambda}{n}=0,
\]
which is one of the contrasts permitted by \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{unif}}\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:vanishing\text{-}variance\text{-}all\text{-}zero\text{-}certificate}\).  Its approximation calculation shows that the maintained primitive and multiplier conditions do not exclude this experiment.  Its all-zero-event calculation is independent of \(t_n\), and yields
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{\mathbb P^{(t)}}\!\left\{
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}
\leq1-e^{-\lambda}<1-\alpha.
\tag{29}
\]
Therefore the required lower limit is strictly below \(1-\alpha\).  The construction does not depend on \(t\), so one experiment works for every schedule.  Neither \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\) nor \(\limsup_n n\kappa_n^3<\infty\) is used for the failure; those conditions simply remain satisfied by the stipulated sequence.  Thus (29) answers the exact OEQ but is not evidence for procedural sharpness of the proposed rare-cell frontier.
